question: What permanent host authorization model should experimental Claws use for manifest-provided stdio MCP commands and reuse of global `mcp.servers` declarations?
rationale: The current patch makes a product/security choice about who may start local commands and who may share a global server; this cannot safely be inferred from implementation mechanics or test coverage.

options.title: Require an approved broker and owner consent
options.body: Allow Claw MCP declarations only through a host-approved command broker or allowlist, and require explicit owner authorization before a different Claw can reuse a global declaration.

options.title: Namespace resources per Claw
options.body: Store declarations under an agent/install-scoped namespace so reuse is impossible unless a separate host-approved sharing mechanism is introduced.

options.title: Defer MCP ownership from this stack
options.body: Land the non-MCP lifecycle stages first and leave MCP declaration ownership out until the execution and sharing policy is approved.

recommendation.title: Require an approved broker and owner consent
recommendation.body: Allow Claw MCP declarations only through a host-approved command broker or allowlist, and require explicit owner authorization before a different Claw can reuse a global declaration.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick-Erichsen is assigned to the PR and has already reviewed the ownership/configuration contract in detail.
